data.one_liner: Flutter data visualization library with linear and radial gauges, scales, ranges, and pointers.
data.what_it_does: Provides customizable Linear Gauge and Radial Gauge (circular gauge) widgets to display data on linear or circular scales. Includes support for axes, ranges, pointers, animations, annotations, and interactive drag behavior.
use_when: You need to display data on a linear scale using a vertical or horizontal layout.
You need to build interactive dashboards with radial/circular gauges and sliders.
You need customizable ranges, markers, needles, and animations for numerical data visualization.
avoid_when: You require a strictly free open-source solution, as this is a commercial package requiring a Syncfusion license.
You only need standard line, bar, or pie charts instead of gauges.
strengths: Rich set of features including animations, smooth interactions, and pointer dragging.
Fully customizable axes, ranges, pointers, and annotations for both linear and radial styles.
Cross-platform support across Android, iOS, web, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
weaknesses: Commercial license required (requires a paid commercial license or free community license).
Large package footprint due to extensive feature set.
data.setup_notes: Requires obtaining a Syncfusion commercial or community license. Simply add the dependency to pubspec.yaml and import the package.

alternatives.name: fl_chart
alternatives.why_pick_it: It is an open-source alternative for charts and data visualization widgets.

alternatives.name: syncfusion_flutter_charts
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a wider variety of charts (line, bar, pie) from the same vendor ecosystem.

alternatives.name: geekyants_flutter_gauges
alternatives.why_pick_it: An open-source alternative package specifically for creating gauges in Flutter.

data.minimal_example:
SfRadialGauge(
  axes: <RadialAxis>[
    RadialAxis(minimum: 0, maximum: 150,
      ranges: <GaugeRange>[
        GaugeRange(startValue: 0, endValue: 50, color: Colors.green),
        GaugeRange(startValue: 50, endValue: 100, color: Colors.orange),
        GaugeRange(startValue: 100, endValue: 150, color: Colors.red)],
      pointers: <GaugePointer>[
        NeedlePointer(value: 90)],
    )
  ]
)
